agyos_skill.intent: Architect and orchestrate persistent AI coworkers (Dots), document workspaces (Spaces & Pages), isolated sandboxes, and human-in-the-loop review gates following OpenDots principles without adding application code.
agyos_skill.instructions: This skill applies the architectural principles and operational logics of CopilotKit OpenDots to AGYOS workflows. It instructs agents how to behave as persistent, role-scoped coworkers operating over structured document workspaces with review checkpoints, without introducing foreign application code or dependencies. Use this skill when: - Designing or operating multi-agent systems where agents must maintain durable identity, context, and background task continuity. - Structuring deliverables into living documents (Spaces and Pages) rather than dumping transient responses into chat logs. - Enforcing human-in-the-loop review gates for high-risk operations (file writes, database operations, external API calls). - Defining isolated compute sandboxes and granular Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool permissions per specialist. 1. **Persistent Coworkers over Ephemeral Chatbots**: An agent ("Dot") is assigned a clear job role, system instructions, and tool bounds. It retains state across task iterations instead of starting fresh each turn. 2. **Spaces and Pages Architecture**: - **Space**: The bounded problem or repository domain. - **Page**: The living document (specifications, architecture designs, audit ledgers, test plans) where deliverables are drafted, refined, and maintained collaboratively. 3. **Per-Worker Isolated Execution**: - Every worker executes within defined sandbox boundaries (dedicated directories, worktrees, or headless browser sessions). - Browser interactions use headless engines (such as Obscura headless CDP) without spawning GUI windows. 4. **Deny-by-Default Review Gates**: - Safe operations (read, query, inspect) run autonomously. - Modifying actions (file writes, deletions, remote pushes, external API calls) pause at explicit review checkpoints presenting the diff, rationale, and rollback path. 5. **Least-Privilege MCP Tool Allowlists**: - Only attach tools explicitly needed for the worker's role. - Reject arbitrary tool access to minimize blast radius. Before assigning work, establish the worker's operational specification: - **Role Title**: Concise job title (e.g. `Security Auditor`, `Performance Optimizer`). - **Scope Boundary**: Files and modules the worker is permitted to inspect or touch. - **Allowed Tools**: Explicit list of read/write tools or MCP actions permitted. - **Execution Mode**: Autonomous for read/analysis; checkpoint-gated for writes.
